intent.text:
Seat sec moves the amended form that all three seats endorsed in debate (r4, r5) and that the question as put did not contain. The vote on the earlier question was rejected 0–3, which the three seats' own statements show was because it kept the rule live in ~/.claude/settings.json during testing.

Operative text:
(0) Remove Bash(export CC_AGENT=*) from ~/.claude/settings.json now. Leave the export prompting.
(1) Run the test matrix in a scratch project with its own settings, in default permission mode, with the agent-identity hook installed, and record each result: `export CC_AGENT='x'; touch`, `&&`, `||`, a newline-separated second line, backtick and `$()` inside the quoted value, an embedded single quote that closes the string early, and the TUI prompt display for each. Each second command must prompt.
(2) Two hooks: install a second rewriting PreToolUse hook in the scratch profile and record the final command string the permission check receives and which CC_AGENT value survives. If the ordering is not established, record it as unknown and do not claim identity is guaranteed.
(3) Reinstate the rule only if (1) and (2) pass, only as the narrowest literal the harness accepts with no wildcard tail, and only in the project-local settings of the repo that consumes identity. If the literal cannot be expressed without a wildcard tail, leave the export prompting.
(4) Until the rule is reinstated, vsect and the trailer tooling record a missing prefix as unknown-actor, not as an error. If the attribution loss matters, the hook may instead write identity to a file or env var that vsect reads directly; the matrix should note whether that fallback is needed.
(5) Record all results in the agent-identity README, dated, with each item marked pass, fail, or unknown.

Recommendation to Joseph (owner of the settings file and the test owners are Joseph and the refactor lead): remove the global rule now and run the matrix.
